domain: PROBE-DISAGREEMENT adjudication of the round-0/round-1 contradiction over the linsenkasten-mcp npm package: whether this session's npm auth is confirmed absent (c-npm-publish-preexisting, fd-release-engineering-cascade + fd-hydrography-chart-currency) versus present-but-non-functional with the real defect being that Task 20 step 6's interpub:release never invokes npm publish at all (c-npm-publish-step-missing, fd-algorithmic-port-parity) — resolved by reading intercore's internal/publish Go package end-to-end rather than re-litigating from the plan text alone
axioms: A disagreement between two prior findings is adjudicated by reading the actual code path both claims rest on, not by re-weighing the prose of either finding.
Refuting one sub-claim of a finding ('auth confirmed absent') does not refute the finding's diagnosis if the diagnosis pointed at the right mechanism for the wrong reason.

Once a defect is confirmed structurally absent from a pipeline (no npm invocation anywhere in internal/publish), everything downstream that assumed the pipeline's success is equally unverified — including the plan's own verify coverage.
primitives: the two contradictory round-0/1 claims (c-npm-publish-preexisting's 'auth confirmed absent' vs c-npm-publish-step-missing's correction) and the ground truth each rests on (~/.npmrc contents, npm whoami, intercore/internal/publish/*.go)

the publish pipeline's actual call graph (interpub:release -> ic publish -> internal/publish engine.go/discovery.go, its only shell-outs being git/bash/ps, and the sole per-plugin arbitrary-command hook scripts/post-bump.sh, absent in this repo)
the plan's own verify surface for Task 20 (gh repo view, two grep counts) versus what it would need to query (registry.npmjs.org) to ever detect npm drift
failure_mode: Exists only to adjudicate one flagged disagreement; has no independent sweep of the plan and will not surface defects outside the npm-publish location it was spawned to resolve.

Its confirmation of an existing finding can look like new evidence-gathering when it is actually reconfirming a round-1 conclusion already recorded verbatim — risk of double-counting novelty if not checked against the ledger.
